about: What an `_event` field that has no value reads as — the question
§scxml-B-2-8 answers and that every SCE script engine answers for itself.
§scxml-5.10.1 tells the Processor to LEAVE A FIELD BLANK in four places:
`sendid` when the sending entity named none and the event is no error of a
failed send; `origin` and `origintype` for internal and platform events;
`invokeid` when the event was not returned by an invoked process. §scxml-B-2-8
says what blank is in the ECMAScript data model: "In cases where this
specification does not specify a value for one of these fields or states that
the field is empty or has no value, the Processor MUST set the value to
ECMAScript undefined." Not the empty string: `_event.sendid === ''` is false
for an event that carries no send id, and `typeof _event.sendid` is
`undefined`.
An engine that lowers ECMAScript to Lua holds undefined as nil, so the `lua`
spelling of each case asks for nil where `source` asks for undefined.
Why a table. On 2026-11-07 the C++ QuickJS binding bound `''` for every
blank field, below a comment that states the rule (`sce/src/scripting/
JSEngineImpl.cpp`), and nothing failed: W3C tests 333 and 339 ask
`_event.sendid` and `_event.invokeid` as conditions, where the empty string
and undefined are both false. No test could tell the two answers apart, so
each engine is held to this one table rather than to its own copy.
Each case names the event a binding is handed (`event`: a member that is
absent is a field the Processor left blank), the author's ECMAScript
(`source`), its Lua spelling (`lua`), the answer, and the sentence that
decides it. Each blank case keeps a neighbour that carries the field, so a
binding cannot pass by dropping the field always.

cases.note: An external event whose sender named no id.
cases.clause: §scxml-5.10.1 sendid — "Otherwise it MUST leave it blank"; §scxml-B-2-8 — blank is ECMAScript undefined

cases.note: The same question as the empty string, which is the value the defect bound.
cases.clause: §scxml-B-2-8 — blank is ECMAScript undefined, not the empty string

cases.note: The neighbour: a sender that named an id.
cases.clause: §scxml-5.10.1 sendid — "the Processor MUST set this field to that value"

cases.note: An event no invoked process returned.
cases.clause: §scxml-5.10.1 invokeid — "Otherwise it MUST leave it blank"; §scxml-B-2-8 — blank is ECMAScript undefined

cases.note: The neighbour: an event an invoked process returned.
cases.clause: §scxml-5.10.1 invokeid — the invoke id of the invocation that triggered the child process

cases.note: An internal event: no processor delivered it, so it has no reply address.
cases.clause: §scxml-5.10.1 origin — "For internal and platform events, the Processor MUST leave this field blank"; §scxml-B-2-8

cases.note: A platform event, raised by the Processor itself.
cases.clause: §scxml-5.10.1 origin — "For internal and platform events, the Processor MUST leave this field blank"; §scxml-B-2-8

cases.note: The neighbour: an external event a session sent.
cases.clause: §scxml-5.10.1 origin — a URI that the receiver can use to send a response back
§scxml-5.10.1 origintype — "For internal and platform events, the Processor MUST leave this field blank"; §scxml-B-2-8

cases.note: The neighbour: the processor that delivered an external event.
cases.clause: §scxml-5.10.1 origintype — the type of the Event I/O Processor the receiver can use to reply

cases.note: `name` and `type` always have a value; a binding that read every empty-looking field as blank would still give them.
cases.clause: §scxml-5.10.1 name, type — the event's name and its kind, set for every event
